## Claims
- [proved] Let \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) be bigrassmannian, \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\), \(t>r+s-n\), and put \(q=n-r\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(q-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\). Let \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[h_1,h_2,\ldots]\) be the integral symmetric-function ring with Schur basis \(\{s_\lambda\}\), \(I_{r,q}=\bigoplus_{\lambda\nsubseteq q^r}\mathbb Zs_\lambda\), \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\), \(A_+=\bigoplus_{d>0}A_d\), and \(J_v=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq q^r}\mathbb Z\bar s_\lambda\subseteq A\). Then both \(G_L=\{\bar s_{(i^j,\rho)}:\rho\subseteq b^a\}\) and \(G_R=\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) map to homogeneous integral bases of \(Q=J_v/A_+J_v\), hence both minimally generate \(J_v\). Consequently \(Q\cong\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^a}\mathbb Ze_\rho\), \(\deg e_\rho=ij+|\rho|\), \(H_Q(z)=z^{ij}\binom{a+b}{a}_z\), and \(Q\) is torsion-free. The pairing \(\langle e_\rho,e_\sigma\rangle=\delta_{\sigma,\rho^\vee}\), \(\rho^\vee=(b-\rho_a,\ldots,b-\rho_1)\), is perfect from \(Q_d\) to \(Q_{2ij+ab-d}\). For \(a=0\), \(b^0\) has the unique empty partition, declared self-complementary. The cited source supplies the lower-family theorem and generation statement [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235], and its no-syzygy mechanism is [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 819-825].
- [unsupported] No parameter-uniform closed formula for a \(G_L\)-to-\(G_R\) transition matrix is asserted.

## Strategy
**Hypotheses and dependencies.** The complete dependencies are `research-attempt-research-plan-task-296-1` (integral lower-family indecomposables, including \(a=0\)); `research-attempt-research-plan-task-301-1` (integral quotient conjugation); `research-attempt-research-plan-task-286-1` (admissible conjugate parameters and transfer to \(G_R\)); and `research-attempt-research-plan-task-317-1` (Hilbert series and complement pairing).

**Proof.** The lower-family generation is source-stated at [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 219-235]. The no-syzygy theorem rules out a nonzero homogeneous relation with nonzero left side [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 819-825]. By `research-attempt-research-plan-task-296-1`, the resulting graded map from the free abelian group on \(G_L\) to \(Q\) has zero kernel, including when \(a=0\). Thus \(G_L\) is an integral homogeneous basis of \(Q\).

By `research-attempt-research-plan-task-301-1`, partition conjugation gives an integral graded quotient isomorphism; by `research-attempt-research-plan-task-286-1`, it preserves \(a,b\) and carries \(G_R(v)\) to the lower family for the conjugate parameters. Hence \(G_R\) is also an integral homogeneous basis of \(Q\). Removing a member of either basis prevents generation of \(Q\), hence of \(J_v\).

Indexing the lower basis by \(\rho\subseteq b^a\) gives the stated Hilbert series. Complementation reverses \(|\rho|\) to \(ab-|\rho|\), so its permutation matrix yields the stated perfect integral pairing.

**Verdict.** The requested target—minimality of exactly both stated families, strengthened to integral homogeneous bases of \(J_v/A_+J_v\)—is established. No transition or finite-computation claim is used.
